problem: "This saves headroom" is ambiguous and reads backwards: a beamless soffit does not save headroom, it adds clear height under the slab (or reduces floor-to-floor height). The body of Section 1 says the opposite idea correctly, so the lead contradicts it.
fix: "A flat soffit gives more clear height under the slab and a clean ceiling, and suits offices and car parks."

problem: The 65 percent negative / 35 percent positive split is stated for any panel. These are the interior-panel proportions; end panels have different proportions, so a student may apply 65/35 to an end panel.
fix: Add: "These 65/35 proportions are for interior panels. End panels have different support and midspan proportions — check the code table for the end panel."

problem: The direct design method is presented as valid for any "regular panel of equal spans". The method has conditions: at least three continuous spans in each direction, longer span to shorter span ratio not more than 2, adjacent span lengths not differing too much, and the clear span lₙ not less than about 0.65 of the centre-to-centre span. Without these, a student will use the method on layouts where it is not allowed.
fix: Add one sentence: "The method is allowed only when there are at least three continuous spans each way, the longer span is not more than twice the shorter span, adjacent spans are nearly equal, and lₙ is not less than about 0.65 of the centre-to-centre span; otherwise use the equivalent frame method."

problem: The critical perimeter is said to lie at half the effective depth from the column face. That is right for a slab without a drop or capital; when a drop or capital is provided, the perimeter is measured from its edge, not from the column face. Since the same section recommends capitals and drops, the statement is incomplete.
fix: Write: "at half the effective depth from the column face — or from the edge of the drop or capital, if one is provided."

problem: The answer gives an unrelated reason: carrying shear near the column is not why the code sends 75 percent of the negative moment to the column strip. The correct reason is the greater stiffness of the band along the column line, which attracts the hogging moment (and this band must deliver that moment to the column).
fix: "The band of slab along the column line is stiff, so it attracts most of the hogging (negative) moment and must transfer it to the column. The code therefore assigns 75 percent of the negative moment to the column strip and 25 percent to the middle strip."
